prompt:
Five molecules in a gas sample have speeds of 200 m s^-1, 300 m s^-1, 400 m s^-1, 500 m s^-1, and 600 m s^-1. Calculate:
(a) the mean speed <c> of the molecules [1]
(b) the root-mean-square speed c_rms of the molecules [1]
hints: In (a), find the simple arithmetic average of the five speeds.
In (b), square each speed, find the average of the squares, and then take the square root.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Direct sum divided by 5 gives 400 m s^-1.
Part (b): Square each value: 40k, 90k, 160k, 250k, 360k. Sum is 900k. Mean is 180k. Square root is 424 m s^-1.
Verify that c_rms (424 m s^-1) is greater than <c> (400 m s^-1).
